subject: Hands-on POC: staging access, allowlist & load window
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC hands-on session + staging prep

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the NovaCorp ML team is excited to move to a hands-on POC. We'd like a two-hour working session where we:
- Walk through prompt sets and expected outputs
- Configure routing/policy rules for production-like requests
- Run a short load test (spike + steady) against a staging endpoint

Availability: next week looks best for us — Tue 4/6 (afternoon PT) or Thu 4/8 (morning PT).

We will need the following from Redwood ahead of time:
- Sandbox API keys scoped to the NovaCorp account (time-limited is fine)
- Staging endpoints and hostnames we should target
- VPC allowlist IP ranges or CIDR to give to our networking team
- Any runbook / checklist to share with our engineers

Also: do you have a recommended load window and a suggested target QPS for the spike tests? We expect to simulate ~150 concurrent connections on our side.

Thanks — copying our ops alias so they can coordinate firewall rules.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Patel | Head of ML Engineering, NovaCorp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC hands-on session + staging prep

Sanjay — great to hear. Tue 4/6 afternoon PT works for our team; we can also do Thu 4/8 morning if you prefer. Suggested plan:

1) 15m intro + goal alignment
2) 45m prompt review & tuning (bring 8–10 canonical prompts)
3) 30m routing & failover walkthrough (policies, model variants)
4) 30m load test + post-mortem

For the load test: we recommend a controlled spike to ~200 QPS for 2 minutes, then a 10-minute steady run at ~60–80 QPS to validate cache behavior and batching. If 150 concurrent connections is what you can generate, we can map that to the QPS target during the runbook.

Pre-reqs from our side: we will provision time-limited sandbox API keys and a staging host; however, we need the CIDR ranges (or a list of public egress IPs) from your networking team to add to the VPC allowlist. Laura (cc'd) will own the runbook and keys. Can you confirm which of the two dates you prefer? Once confirmed we’ll send the invite and the preliminary runbook.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@novacorp.com, IT Team <it@novacorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC hands-on session + staging prep

Thanks Jonas — we’ll take Tue 4/6 afternoon PT. Our ops team will open a firewall change ticket once we have the target allowlist. For now, our expected egress ranges (public) are:
- 18.72.128.0/22
- 52.45.16.0/24
- 35.180.200.0/23

Please let us know if you need CIDR-style ranges or specific IPs; we can also coordinate a temporary VPN if that’s easier for you.

On prompts: we’ll bring 12 prompts spanning multi-turn chat and structured-output cases (JSON). For the load test we can drive 150 concurrent connections that will produce ~120–180 QPS depending on token size.

Sanjay
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novacorp.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC hands-on session + staging prep

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the ranges. We can work with those CIDRs; Laura will request your ops team’s ticket # for our records. Attached are two artifacts: redwood-poc-runbook-v1.pdf (session checklist + step-by-step load test instructions) and allowlist-template.txt (format your ticket can paste). A few notes before the session:

- API keys: we’ll issue two time-limited sandbox API keys (one for your testers, one for programmatic load tools). Keys will expire 72 hours after the session unless extended.
- Staging endpoints: we will provide a short hostname (staging-novacorp.redwood.ai) and an ALIAS you can swap into your test harness.
- Prompt review: please attach the 12 prompts to this thread by EOD 4/6 so our prompt engineer can pre-seed examples and suggested system messages.
- Load test targets: unless you ask otherwise, we’ll run the spike to 200 QPS for 90s, then 10 minutes at 80 QPS. If that looks risky, we can scale back.

Action items for NovaCorp before the call:
- Paste the final allowlist ticket or a CIDR confirmation
- Attach the prompt set (JSON or docx)
- Confirm the preferred tool for the load test (k6, Locust, or internal)

We’ll send the calendar invite in the next message.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>

- NovaCorp: attach prompts + firewall ticket ID before 17:00 PT on 4/6
- Redwood: provision sandbox keys and staging host by 09:00 PT on 4/6; upload runbook to shared drive
- Load test: we’ll use k6 unless you confirm a different tool

Links: runbook in shared workspace: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bPOC-Workspace
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-4821 (internal)

If everything’s good I’ll lock the invite for Tue 2027-04-06 13:00–15:00 PT. Looking forward to the session — we’ll be prepared to walk through prompt engineering, routing policies, and live traffic shaping during the load window.

Thanks,
Jonas
